notes: I read the landing page and the demo report on my phone, top to bottom. The top cards tell me what I need in ten seconds: 9 extra lunch customers a day, worst case €560, 37% of my spare cash (report-phone.png; report.txt:55-69). The point about regulars is new to me: each one who switches costs me €1.32, so €15 a day before anyone new comes (report.txt:870). That is the real lesson. I could tape the test card by the till: tally sheet, a deal button, 'Do you usually have lunch here?' (report.txt:821-830). Nowhere does it say 'AI predicts', and I believe the sums because I can redo them. What holds it back: to use my own numbers I have to 'turn on Developer mode' or paste an 'MCP server' URL (landing.txt:154,174). That is where I would stop. One box says an AI played the customers, and the next one says 'no AI' (report.txt:516,524), so I don't know what the AI did. The headline −€56.02 doesn't match 12.40×10−180 in 'Why this changed' (report.txt:489). The €370 stop line counts 'discounts to regulars', and those are not in my receipts (report.txt:839,858). I'd notice these gaps. They are more than polish.
improvements: Report demo banner ('Swap in your own to get your answer', report.txt:7) and landing hero: a café owner has no way to get her own numbers in without 'Developer mode' or an 'MCP server' URL (landing.txt:154,174). Give her a plain 'Use your own numbers' route she can finish alone. Either an in-page form for the 8 facts and 4 guesses that rewrites the report link, or a one-screen guide put first ('In Claude: Settings → Connectors → paste this, 4 taps'), with ChatGPT developer mode, Cursor and VS Code moved behind 'For developers'. Criterion: feasible on Monday / would she use it. It worked when Selin can reach a report with her own 140 customers and €7.40 from her phone without asking her nephew.

Step 5 rehearsal (report.txt:516 vs 524): 'These are imagined customers played by an AI from short descriptions' sits one box above 'Played by simple fixed rules, with no AI'. Show only the statement that is true for this run, and add one line: what the AI did here (nothing, or played the customers) and what plain code did (all the money sums). Criterion: learning about AI, honesty. It worked when report.txt holds one consistent statement and Selin can answer 'what did the AI do in this report?'

Short answer, Step 3 'Expected' and 'Why this changed' (report.txt:61, 329, 489): the arithmetic shown, 8 × €6.30 − €38.00 = €12.40 a day, then ×10 − €180, gives −€56.00, but the headline says −€56.02. Show test results in whole euros ('about −€56'), or carry the unrounded switching cost (€15.0024) into the maths line. Criterion: believing the numbers. It worked when a phone-calculator check of 'Why this changed' reproduces the headline exactly.

Test card cost cap (report.txt:817, 824, 844, 858): 'spent €370 … (setup, staff, promotion and discounts to regulars)' can't be read from the receipts envelope (report.txt:839). Make the stop line something she counts: 'On day 5, if you average fewer than 5 extra lunch customers a day, stop. By then the test has cost about €370.' Or add 'regulars' part = strokes in the "usually has lunch here" column × €1.32'. Also give one baseline instruction: 'one week before you start' (report.txt:820) vs 'for 3 weekdays' (report.txt:876). It worked when every number on the card can be filled in from the tally sheet, the till's Z-report and the envelope.

Step 2 'What your numbers already say' (report.txt:238-246): '€15,287 left after ingredients (weekdays)' sits next to '€16,500 fixed costs' with no comment. It reads like 'this café already loses €1,200 a month', and that scared me. Add one line ('weekends are not counted here, so this is not your whole month'), or take fixed costs out of that list. It worked when an owner reading it does not think the demo café is failing.

Step 5 summary vs Step 3: the sums' likely guess is 8 extra a day, but the rehearsal shows 'Tried it 0 of 6' and 'Told someone 0 of 6' (report.txt:535-540). Meanwhile the landing promised 'Mia told Jonas' and '3 of 6 tried it' (landing.txt:129,140). Add one bridging sentence under 'How far it spread': 'Your sums assume 8 extra a day; here no imagined customer tried it. That is a doubt to check in the test, not a forecast.' Make the landing sample match the demo too. It worked when Selin does not read the rehearsal as 'the AI says nobody will come'.
understood: Break-even: I need 9 extra lunch customers every weekday of the 10-day test to get back what the test costs, the €180 sign and flyers included. If I keep the deal afterwards, 7 extra a day is enough not to lose money.
The most the test can cost me: €560, if nobody new comes. That is 37% of the €1,500 I could spare, and 63% is left over.
The guess that matters most is how many extra people come. 3 a day or 15 a day changes the result by €756, so that is what I count.
Every regular who swaps their usual €11.20 lunch for the €9.90 deal costs me €1.32. With about 11 of them that is €15 a day before anyone new arrives. I had not thought of that.
The test card: a tally sheet by the till, a deal button on the till, ask 'Do you usually have lunch here?', and decide keep / tweak / stop before I see the results.
The six customers are made up. They gave me questions to ask real people (vegetarian every day? does the soup change?), not numbers.

wouldTry: maybe, because I could run the test card on paper next Monday: the tally sheet, the deal button and the keep / tweak / stop rule make sense to me. But these are a made-up café's numbers, and to get mine in I would have to turn on 'Developer mode' in ChatGPT or paste a connector URL into settings. I would need my nephew for that. And I couldn't tell when I had 'spent €370', because part of it is regulars' discounts I never see in receipts.
learnedAboutAI: The money sums are plain arithmetic I can check myself (8 × €6.30 = €50.40), labelled 'Calculated', and not done by the AI. The extra customers and the 30% of regulars switching are guesses, labelled 'A guess', and only the real test answers them. The six customers are imagined: good for finding questions like 'Is there a vegetarian option every day?', never counted in the money. The page also tells me, in two boxes next to each other, that an AI played them and that no AI did, so I am not sure what the AI actually did in this report.
